summary:
This joint resolution says U.S. Armed Forces must be removed from fighting in or against Iran unless Congress clearly approves it. Congress could approve it by declaring war or by passing a specific law that allows military force.

The bill says Congress has the power to declare war. It also says the President has the duty to defend the United States, its people, service members, diplomats, and places from attack. The bill states that Congress has not declared war on Iran or passed a specific law allowing force in or against Iran.

If this becomes law, the President would have to stop any U.S. military fighting in or against Iran that Congress has not approved.

The bill also says what it does not stop. It would still allow the United States to defend against attacks on the U.S. or its people and facilities in other countries. It would allow intelligence work. It would also allow help to countries attacked by Iran since February 28, 2026, including help stopping attacks or giving defensive supplies.
